questions.question: Does `opencode acp` answer `initialize` with protocol version 1, and which capabilities and auth methods does it state?
questions.summary: It answers protocolVersion 1 with agentCapabilities loadSession true, mcpCapabilities {http, sse}, promptCapabilities {embeddedContext, image} and sessionCapabilities {close, fork, list, resume}, one auth method `opencode-login` ("Run `opencode auth login` in the terminal"), and agentInfo OpenCode 1.18.30.

questions.question: Does stdout carry only JSON-RPC frames, with and without `--print-logs`, and where do the logs go?
questions.summary: Stdout carried only JSON-RPC frames in every run, with and without --print-logs (frameStats.nonJsonStdoutLines is 0 in every record), and with --print-logs --log-level WARN the log lines go to stderr and also to $XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/log/opencode.log (S1f, S4), but where they go without --print-logs was not shown: stderr stayed empty and the log file was empty in the 1 s S0 runs both with and without the flag; a refused request also prints an "Error handling request" dump on stderr.

questions.question: Which directory does a session work in when `session/new.cwd`, `--cwd`, the spawn cwd and `$PWD` differ, and does the agent read, write and run commands itself there when the client advertises no `fs` and no `terminal`?
questions.summary: The session works in session/new.cwd: with --cwd, the spawn cwd and $PWD naming three other directories, the agent's `pwd` printed <scratch>/wt and the shim started in <scratch>/wt; with no fs and no terminal capability the agent never sent an fs/* or terminal/* request in any run, and ran commands (S1d, S3), wrote greeting.txt and committed it (S1b) with its own tools.

questions.question: Does a stdio server named in `session/new.mcpServers` start; with which environment (the listed variables, the parent's, both); under which parent process; and under which names does the model see its tools?
questions.summary: It starts during session/new (the shim recorded initialize and tools/list in every S0 run, which sent no prompt) as a child of the `opencode acp` process in the client's process group, with both environments: OpenCode's own (the client's PROBE_MARKER) plus the listed entries (PROBE_FROM_SESSION), plus AGENT, OPENCODE, OPENCODE_CLIENT, OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT, OPENCODE_PID, OPENCODE_PURE and npm_config_user_agent that OpenCode adds (and OPENCODE_PRINT_LOGS and OPENCODE_LOG_LEVEL under --print-logs, S0-good-logs); the model sees the tools as orchestrator_heartbeat, orchestrator_block, orchestrator_inbox, orchestrator_log and orchestrator_report (the tool_call titles).

questions.question: When that server's command cannot start, is it an error of `session/new`, a failed prompt, or a turn without the tools?
questions.summary: A turn without the tools: session/new answers normally (S0-badshim, S1f), stderr gets `level=WARN message="server unavailable" key=orchestrator type=local status=failed` only under --print-logs, and in S1f the prompt ended end_turn with the model replying NO-TOOL; no frame says the server is missing.

questions.question: Is the `block` call answered after 75 s cut for a server passed over ACP, and does a per-launch setting (`OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` with `mcp.orchestrator.timeout`) lift the limit?
questions.summary: Yes and yes: with no timeout setting (S1) every `block` call failed at 60 s with "MCP error -32001: Request timed out" although the shim answered at 75 s; a disabled `mcp.orchestrator` entry in OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT carrying only `timeout: 900000` (S1b) lifted the limit for the server passed over ACP, so both 75 s `block` calls completed with the answer, and that entry's own command never started (configShimCalls 0); and `experimental.mcp_timeout: 900000` (S1b-exp) did the same.
commands: grep -o '"text":"MCP error -32001: Request timed out"' test/fixtures/acp/opencode/frames/S1.jsonl | wc -l

questions.question: Does `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` (the permission ruleset, `snapshots: false`, `share: disabled`, `model`) apply to a session of `opencode acp`?
questions.summary: The permission ruleset applies (the `ask` rules of S2-S4 produced session/request_permission, the `deny` rule of S1 refused `sleep 60` naming the rules), and a valid `model` applies (S0-model: currentValue opencode/nemotron-3.5-lightning-free), but an unknown `model` is dropped without a word (S7), and whether `snapshots: false` and `share: disabled` apply was not shown (no run went without them, and the one data directory listed, S1's, belongs to a run that edited no file).
commands: grep -o 'The user has specified a rule which prevents you[^\\]*' test/fixtures/acp/opencode/frames/S1.jsonl | head -1

questions.question: Under a rule that asks, does the agent send `session/request_permission`, with which options and which fields naming the command; and are the shim's tools asked for or pre-approved by `"orchestrator_*": "allow"`?
questions.summary: Under bash `"*": "ask"` the agent sends session/request_permission with the options once/allow_once "Allow once", always/allow_always "Always allow" and reject/reject_once "Reject" (no reject_always), naming the command in toolCall.title and toolCall.rawInput.command (kind execute); orchestrator_heartbeat ran with no request, pre-approved by "orchestrator_*": "allow", and a `deny` rule sends no request at all.

questions.question: After `reject_once`, does the model get an error and the turn go on, or does the turn end as it does under `opencode run`? After `allow_once`, does the command run? With no answer, what does the turn do within 120 s?
questions.summary: After reject_once the tool call is marked failed ("The user rejected permission to use this specific tool call.") and session/prompt answers end_turn 4 ms later with no model step between, so the turn ends as under `opencode run` and the model never sees the error (no FALLBACK-OK); after allow_once `uname -s` ran and the model replied Darwin; with no answer the turn sent no frame for 120 s (frameStats.maxGapMs 120005) until session/cancel, after which the tool failed and the prompt answered cancelled.

questions.question: How does a turn end: the `stopReason`; whether the process stays up afterwards; what ends it (closing stdin, SIGTERM); with which exit code?
questions.summary: A completed turn ends with the session/prompt result `stopReason: end_turn` and a `usage` object; the agent stays up after the turn until the client closes its stdin, then exits with code 0 (agentExit.how stdinClosed after every completed turn, S1b, S2, S3, S1d, S7), while SIGTERM to the group ends it by the signal (code null, signal SIGTERM) before it answers the prompt.

questions.question: Does `session/cancel` during a 60 s shell command end the turn with `cancelled`, how soon, and do the command's process and the shim's process end?
questions.summary: session/cancel sent 10 s into `sleep 60` was answered `stopReason: cancelled` 15 ms later (frames t 13682 and 13697), the `sleep` process ended (no orphan), and the shim stayed up with the session until the agent's stdin was closed, then exited by itself.

questions.question: Does SIGTERM to the client's process group during a turn leave a process; what is left after SIGKILL of that group; and does a client started as `SubprocessRunner` starts an agent (detached, stdin ignored, stdout and stderr in one file) finish its turn after its parent has exited?
questions.summary: Both signals leave the bash tool's `sleep 60`, which OpenCode starts in a process group of its own (pgid = its pid), while the client, `opencode acp` and the shim are in the client's group and end (the shim recorded the SIGTERM); the probe had to kill the `sleep` both times (orphans); a client started detached with stdin ignored and stdout and stderr in one file finished its turn (DONE, exit 0, no orphan) after its parent had exited.

questions.question: Which usage does ACP carry (the fields of `usage_update`, a `usage` on the prompt response, a cost), and how does it compare with the tokens and cost `opencode run --format json` reports for the same prompt?
questions.summary: The prompt response carries `usage` {inputTokens, outputTokens, totalTokens, thoughtTokens, cachedReadTokens} and one `usage_update` {used, size, cost {amount, currency}} arrives at the end of the turn, but both describe the last step (the last assistant message) only, not the turn: for the task prompt ACP reported 996 input, 35 output and 9984 cache-read tokens where `opencode run --format json` summed 11041, 1419 and 99328 over 14 steps (its last step alone was 720, 28 and 8960); cost was 0 both ways (free model), and ACP reports no step or turn count.

questions.question: How are the model and the effort chosen for a session: an option in the `session/new` answer, a set-model method, or only configuration?
questions.summary: All three for the model: the session/new answer carries configOptions `model` (a select with currentValue and the options) and `mode` (build, plan); session/set_model and session/set_config_option {configId: "model"} both take a model, and refuse an unknown one with -32602 "Invalid params: model not found"; `model` in OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT sets the default; no effort option is offered for these models and set_config_option {configId: "effort"} answers -32602 "effort not found: high"; the list of options differed between two fresh starts ("OpenCode/…" against "OpenCode Zen/…" names).

questions.question: How do an unknown model, a server that did not start and a rejected permission show in the frames and on stderr, and can the reasons of `classifyOpenCodeFailure` be told apart?
questions.summary: An unknown model in the configuration shows nowhere (S7 ran the default model, empty stderr), while one set over ACP is a JSON-RPC error -32602 "model not found" plus an "Error handling request" dump on stderr; a server that did not start shows only as the WARN `server unavailable key=orchestrator` on stderr under --print-logs (which the mcpStartupFailed pattern matches); a rejected permission shows only in the frames (a failed tool_call_update with "The user rejected permission…" and end_turn), with no `auto-rejecting` line; so mcpStartupFailed can be told apart, unknownModel only when the client sets the model itself, permissionDenied only from the frames, and authFailed was not probed (the free model needs no login).

questions.question: What does the stream show while the agent waits: are there frames during the 75 s tool call, and what is the longest gap between two frames of the task run?
questions.summary: Nothing arrives while a tool call runs: in S1b each 75 s `block` call left a gap with no frame of 75017 and 75159 ms (the longest), in S1 the cut calls left 60 s gaps, and in S4 the unanswered permission request left 120005 ms; progress otherwise streams as session/update frames (thought and message chunks, tool_call and tool_call_update) as the agent works.

questions.question: Of 8 clients started in the same instant on one data directory, with no prompt sent, how many fail `initialize` or `session/new`, and with which message?
questions.summary: None: all 8 clients started together on one XDG_DATA_HOME answered initialize and session/new and exited 0 in 1.6-2.6 s, with no `database is locked` line on any stderr.

questions.question: Does the agent commit on the launch branch in the linked worktree, and is the fake token found under the data directory or in the logs after the run?
questions.summary: The agent committed greeting.txt as dbe1709 "Add greeting file" on task/PROBE/l1 in the linked worktree <scratch>/wt and left it clean (S1b; S9 did the same through `opencode run`); the fake token was never found under the run's XDG data, state, cache or config directories nor on stderr: passed in the session/new `env` it is in the client's frames file only (S1, S1b), and passed through `--orch-env-file` (S1e) it is nowhere but the shim's own record, so the env file keeps it out of the frames as well.

command: <parent: spawn sh -c <client> detached, stdin ignored, stdout+stderr to launch.log, exit>
